inventory.caption: Controlled mutation separates a proposed edit from its effects. Supported operations resolve targets against current state and pass selected guards before mutation. Per-operation results include refusals; successful session operations and remediation-pass mutations use distinct attribution channels. A comparison affects admission only when its consumer refuses the prohibited edit; any direct write path lies outside this boundary.
inventory.conversion: Author-approved diagnostic-evidence label distinguishes advisory before-value comparison from selected admission guards; target-resolution width adjusts to give the edge label room.
inventory.svg_title: Controlled mutation separates proposals from effects
inventory.svg_description: A flexible producer emits a typed proposal. The resolver uses the document structure model of current artifact state. A before-value comparison reports mismatches by default; it is not the hard admission gate. Within the controlled application boundary, the supported operation vocabulary and selected guards determine whether the applier may mutate the resolved target. Per-operation results include refusal and failure. Successful session edits and remediation-pass mutations produce distinct attribution records. Unmigrated direct edits remain outside this route.

inventory.caption: Substitutable reasoning. Two alternative engines use a domain’s task and operation models while making different planning decisions. Model selection chooses a foundation model within an engine; controlled application and acceptance consume their own models and evidence. Type compatibility preserves the request form, not semantic quality or equivalent behavior.
inventory.conversion: Author-approved cleanup groups exactly two engines and places shared model selection outside that group. The capability input is prominent; acceptance visibly consumes findings and policy.
inventory.svg_title: Substitutable reasoning with stable domain obligations
inventory.svg_description: Task and workflow models guide two alternative engines: a pass-graph executor or a planning agent. Capability and selection knowledge informs model choice within an engine. Both engines produce typed proposals governed by an operation model and applied to the current artifact through a controlled application boundary. Separate evaluation and an acceptance model guide acceptance. Restricting mutation authority requires more than a typed request interface.

inventory.caption: Governed delegation joins an assignment to relevant knowledge, durable work, and acceptance evidence. Context selection is bounded and advisory. Dispatch gates act on assignment structure and resolved phase state; completion review evaluates landed work and independent evidence. Recovery preserves existing artifacts before work is reassigned.
inventory.conversion: Author-approved moderate redraw aligns the two governance decisions with equal heavy diamonds. Independent checks produce review evidence; durable work also reaches completion review. Refusal, positive DONE and recovery semantics remain.
inventory.svg_title: Governed delegation with parallel dispatch and completion decisions
inventory.svg_description: The work order and component/constraint models feed bounded context selection. Lifecycle policy and reconciled phase state feed the dispatch decision: is the assignment authorized? A refused assignment does not execute without repair or a valid override. An authorized agent preserves durable work, which is both inspected at completion and evaluated by independent checks. Checks produce review evidence; the completion decision asks whether obligations are satisfied. Interrupted or unresolved work is inspected and reconciled before redispatch. Absence of state is not evidence of DONE.

inventory.caption: Model-based regression-test selection. Component and dependency models derive affected subsystems, and validation coverage maps them to checks. Execution records and findings feed an acceptance gate under an explicit policy. Dependency analyses and full-suite comparisons challenge the selection; conservative fallback covers recognized uncertainty, not every unmodeled dependency.
inventory.conversion: Author-approved dashed feedback returns model revision to component/dependency and validation-coverage models; recognized-gap fallback and challenge evidence retain their distinct roles.
inventory.svg_description: Component and declared dependency models derive a change-impact model: the affected subsystems. Validation coverage maps the affected set to selected checks. The validation execution model supplies modes and interpretation policy; actual execution produces records and findings for acceptance. Recognized gaps widen execution to the full suite. Separate dependency and coverage evidence plus full-run comparisons challenge selection, leading to revised models or broader validation; these observations do not prove universal completeness.
